raw_response:
*settles into the thinking of a 76-year-old man who has farmed this same land for half a century*

---

Ai, another year. My back's not what it was at sixty, but the land still needs tending. My son drives trucks now — he's gone most of the season, sends money home. My daughter-in-law helps when she can, but she has the children. So it's mostly me, my wife, and the oldest grandchild on weekends.

Twelve mu. I've had the same twelve mu for thirty years. Eight mu I do wheat then maize — that's the main thing, that's our grain. The other four mu I keep in cotton. Cotton's hard work at picking time but the price is okay, and I'm used to it.

**Wheat (8 mu) — I plant around October 8th or so**

I always plant around Hanlu, after the dew comes cold. My grandfather planted then, my father planted then, I plant then. Last year I planted a bit late because the maize wasn't quite ready to harvest and I wasted three days. This year I won't let that happen — I'll get the grandson to help pull the old maize stalks faster.

For seed, I saved from last year's harvest. The village seed shop sells the new varieties but they cost money and last year mine was fine — 430 jin per mu, roughly. Not bad. I'll save seed again.

Fertilizer — I put down one big bag of diammonium phosphate before plowing it in. That's the base. Then when the wheat starts jointing, maybe late February or early March when you can see it's heading up, I scatter half a bag of urea per mu. That's what I've done for twenty years. My neighbor Old Zhang does the same. One year my son told me to use more — he read something — but I didn't see the difference so I went back to my way.

Water: I pump three times. Once right after planting to help it establish — very important, the ground is dry in October. Once at jointing. Once at heading. Any more and it costs too much to run the pump. Each time costs money, maybe 30 yuan per mu with the electricity and the water fee.

I do no-till on the wheat ground because I'm getting old and turning the soil by hand is too much. I hire someone with a small tractor for base tillage. Costs about 50 yuan per mu but saves my back.

---

**Maize (8 mu) — right after wheat harvest, mid-June**

This is the part that always makes me nervous. Wheat comes off early June and I have maybe five, six days to get the maize in before the window closes. The ground is hot and hard. I hire a seeder — 40 yuan per mu — because I can't plant 8 mu by hand fast enough at my age. I buy hybrid seed from the village shop. Last year I used Xianyu 335, I know how it grows, I'll use it again. About 4 kg per mu.

For fertilizer on maize, I put everything in at once when I plant — one bag compound fertilizer per mu, mix it in. My son says I should topdress too but honestly by August I'm tired and the rain usually comes anyway. If it's a dry summer I'll pump once, maybe twice. Last year we got decent rain so I only pumped once.

Maize I expect around 480-500 jin per mu. Some years more, some years less depending on the rain in July and August.

---

**Cotton (4 mu) — plant around April 20th**

Cotton is old habit. When I was young, half the village grew cotton. Now most switched to wheat-maize because it's easier. I keep four mu because I know how to do it and the picking money in autumn is real cash, which I like.

I plant transplanted seedlings — I start seeds in a seedbed in early April, then transplant around the 20th. This is a lot of work but cotton is fragile when young. I use simple fertilizer, one bag compound per mu spread over the season in two applications — one when it starts to branch, one when bolls are setting. Maybe some urea if the leaves look pale.

I irrigate cotton twice, maybe three times if July is very dry. Cotton doesn't like too much water anyway.

Picking is the hard part. Four mu of cotton is maybe twenty picking days over September and October. My wife and I can do it but it takes time. The grandchildren help on holidays.

I expect around 200-250 jin lint per mu. Not great but it covers costs and gives me some cash.
